subject.title: subagent sessions don't trigger session-memory hook

question: Which lifecycle contract should bundled session-memory use for completed subagent sessions: direct subagent_ended handling, a generic internal session-end hook, or typed plugin session_end?
rationale: Current main exposes multiple adjacent lifecycle surfaces, and a one-off handler branch could create duplicate or incompatible session-memory behavior without a maintainer-owned contract.

options.title: Use a generic session-end contract
options.body: Make completed subagent sessions produce the same durable session-end semantics used by other session finalization paths, then have session-memory consume that contract.

options.title: Handle subagent_ended in session-memory
options.body: Add a narrow bundled-hook path for subagent completion, accepting that session-memory owns subagent transcript and workspace resolution details directly.

options.title: Defer bundled behavior
options.body: Leave session-memory scoped to command resets and direct users to external plugins for subagent completion memory until the broader plugin lifecycle design lands.

recommendation.title: Use a generic session-end contract
recommendation.body: Make completed subagent sessions produce the same durable session-end semantics used by other session finalization paths, then have session-memory consume that contract.

likelyOwner.reason: This is primarily a hooks/plugin lifecycle contract decision, and recent session-memory plus related hook review history points here most strongly.
